image_description: A composite image showing two distinct marine organisms on rocky substrates. The left panel displays two green, oval-shaped mollusks with segmented dorsal shells (chitons) clinging to a rock. The right panel shows a cluster of white, volcano-shaped crustaceans (barnacles) attached to a rock surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is reduced without eyes or tentacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior ends of the green organisms on the left are blunt and lack any visible protruding sensory structures like eyes or tentacles, consistent with chiton anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior end is blunt and indistinct.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the shell plates curves smoothly into the girdle without a distinct head shape.
No antennae or eye stalks are visible on the dorsal surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal surface protected by eight overlapping calcareous plates arranged in linear series.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The green organisms clearly exhibit the characteristic eight transverse plates (valves) running from head to tail, embedded in the surrounding tissue.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plates embedded in tough leathery girdle that may be smooth, spiny, or hairy.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, textured girdle surrounds the central plates, appearing somewhat granular or spiny, which matches the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plate coloration ranges from grey, brown, green to mottled patterns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The chitons on the left are dark green with lighter mottling/stripes on the plates, fitting the coloration criteria.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface features broad muscular foot for adhesion to rocky substrates.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a dorsal view; the ventral foot is completely occluded by the body and the rock surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits dorsoventrally flattened profile when clinging to surfaces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The organisms conform tightly to the irregular rock surface, exhibiting a low, flattened profile typical of chitons.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a behavioral trait not observable in a static image where the animals are firmly attached.

The boundary between the chiton girdle and the rock substrate on the left is slightly muddy, with some texture bleeding, though it remains largely coherent.

The subjects on the left perfectly match all testable anatomical checkpoints: eight dorsal plates, leathery girdle, reduced head, and flattened profile. Although the right panel contains barnacles (a different class), the presence of clear, high-fidelity chitons satisfies the primary classification requirement. Un-testable checkpoints (ventral foot) were correctly ignored.
